<pb n="170"/>...is taught. Up to this point, the **Compiler** has shown the greatness of the self and the subject matter of the chapter along with the oral instructions. Regarding the phrase "because the body, speech, and mind have become one," it means that if all things are analyzed from the perspective of ultimate reality, they are not perceived as separate. That which dwells in one’s own continuum is precisely what dwells in the continuum of another. However, based on the distinction between the object to be accomplished and the accomplisher, "subjugation" for the sake of reversing adventitious stains means the practitioner subjugates the object to be accomplished. This is also a symbolic term; through peaceful activities and so forth, they are also cared for. Regarding the phrase "A-li Ka-li" <note>vowels and consonants</note> and so forth, it shows the meditative concentration that is beautiful because it completes the collection of activities such as peaceful ones through mantras interspersed with the three syllables <note>Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ</note> which condense all mantras of the nature of the body and so forth. "That which shows it" refers to whatever collection of sounds clarifies it in that way. Regarding "explained with intention," this is because reality is shown through the gateway of contradictory language. From the *Tikā Commentary Clarifying the Lamp* <note>original: "sgron ma gsal bar byེད་ pa'i 'grel pa'i ṭī kā"</note>, this concludes the extensive explanation of the fourteenth chapter.

The explanation of the fifteenth chapter begins with the phrase "The explained and the unexplained" and so forth. The intention is this: what was "explained" was taught in the thirteenth and fourteenth chapters. What was "unexplained" are the collections of activities to be explained in the fifteenth, sixteenth, and seventeenth chapters; because these will not be accomplished without the illusion-like meditative concentration, the fifteenth chapter is taught. Regarding the phrase "possessing the nature of the four emptinesses," these are: emptiness, extreme emptiness, great emptiness, and all-emptiness. Alternatively: appearance, increase of appearance, near-attainment of appearance, and clear light. Alternatively: the four channels within the lotus. The "self" <note>essence</note> is the central channel, the "parasol of desire." As it is said:
<pb n="171"/>
"In the center of the <term>bhaga</term> <gloss>source of phenomena/womb</gloss> is the space, adorned with five spaces; possessing a navel and filaments, it is beautiful with eight petals." Thus it appears. Regarding "indestructible," this is because it is the essence of the **Dharma Body**. "All empowerments" refers to the master, the secret, and the wisdom empowerments. The "empowerment of those" refers to the wisdom-gnosis, which is characterized by the phrase "the fourth is likewise." Because he is the essence of that, **Vajradhara** is called "the empowerment of all." All the families divided by the inclinations of sentient beings are the hundred, the five, or the three families. As it is said: "The families are explained as being of a hundred types; condensed, they are of five types; through the division of body, speech, and mind, they later become three types." The **Blessed One**, who is the nature of those, is so because he emanates them. Therefore, the word "knowing" means "emanating." "Indivisible speech" refers to speech characterized by union with a <term>mudrā</term> <gloss>consort/seal</gloss>. "Explained without intention" means showing reality very clearly. "Conduct without proliferation" is the nature of entering into union with a <term>mudrā</term> through the gateway of all such conduct. From the phrase "the outcaste woman" down to "because it is the yoga of conceptualization," it refers to the practitioners of **Akṣobhya**, **Vairocana**, and **Amitābha** in due order. In a place secluded from people, smeared with cow dung and the like, one should draw a wheel of the nature of the support and the supported, or meditate on it with the mind. In its center, one places a well-trained, beautiful, and well-adorned girl of one's own family: an outcaste, a laundry-maid, or a dancer, aged twelve, twenty, or sixteen. They are associated with the blue, red, or white water-lily <note>original: "utpala"</note>, and are pervaded by the five families. Having placed them and preceded by passion and offerings, one should dwell having performed the application <note>of the rites</note> through the stage of withdrawal.
<pb n="172"/>
Likewise, the practitioners of **Ratnasambhava** and **Amoghasiddhi** should also dwell having accomplished laundry-maids and outcaste girls, condensed from the families of delusion and hatred. Regarding "the practitioner who has entered thus," it means one who has exerted effort in the conduct without proliferation. "The nature of **Amitābha**" means the text teaches that whoever meditates on the meditative concentration of **Amitābha** will become like him. Since it is a symbolic illustration, it means that the practitioners of **Akṣobhya** and the others will also become like them. "Will dwell on the ten stages" means becoming the master of the ten stages. "Holding the Lord of Speech" shows the benefits of the **Amitābha** yoga. The Lord of Mind and the Lord of Body should be understood for the yogis of **Akṣobhya** and **Vairocana**; likewise, the Treasury of Space and the Performer of All Activities should be explained for the yogis of **Ratnasambhava** and **Amoghasiddhi**. The text shows this by saying "by possessing that yoga, one becomes like that." "Possessing the supreme lordships" means possessing the lordship of the body and so forth. "All sentient beings" means being distinguished from all sentient beings because one is supreme among one's own and other groups. "Becoming a universal monarch" <term>cakravartin</term> means becoming the master of the circle of the mandala. "Because of being a practitioner of the yoga of conceptualization" means by meditating on the generation stage. After showing the divisions of the <term>mudrās</term> of the generation stage yoga in this way, the text then says "it should also be shown to those who dwell in the completion stage." From the phrase "the four families" down to "it will be achieved before long," it shows that a practitioner of the completion stage should take a girl of any of the families, such as a **Brahmin**, and through the sequence of union, experience the three gnoses—appearance and so forth—arising from causes and conditions. One should dwell focusing on the Vajra Body which is the union of the nature of the unlocalized nirvana arising from the stages of manifest enlightenment of the external and internal self.
<pb n="173"/>
To show that specifically, "any one of the four families" is said because for those dwelling in the completion stage, there is no conceptualization. "Having taken" means having taken her as a companion in practice. "Possessing that realization" means attaining the deity's body through the completion stage. "That is **Vajradhara**" means because he has become the fruit of everything. "Completing that" means generating the meditative concentration of union. "Having completed it through the stages of manifest enlightenment" means through the two stages. This method is the cause for the accomplishment of the **Great Seal** <term>Mahāmudrā</term>. "When the red boundary is cut and passed" means at dusk, because at that time the sun sets. Therefore, at the time when night falls, the master dwelling in the center of the mandala should perform the ritual of the gathering-circle <term>gaṇacakra</term> with the five types of offerings and so forth, preceded by a prayer for the sake of attaining reality. Then, after the offerings, in the middle of the night, having received the empowerment of wisdom following the secret empowerment from the master who has become pure, one's own family is shown. One "receives empowerment through the arising of bliss." By that very taste, at the time when dawn breaks and the light appears, when the supreme driver of the sun appears, the parts of the night have passed. To show that, "at the time of the rising sun" means first the driver of the sun, the dawn, appears, and then the sun itself rises. At that time, through the instructions on the stages of manifest enlightenment, accomplishment will be attained.
<pb n="174"/>
Regarding the "stages of external manifest enlightenment," these are the instructions characterized by the realization of reality in relation to external time. In order to show the internal, the internal stages of manifest enlightenment are taught. "Gnosis of method" is the gnosis of the increase of appearance, named "passion." Because it is illustrated by union, it is the nature of union. "Having arisen" means having generated that. "Setting" means having passed. "Having become the essence of wisdom" refers to the arising and dissolving after the gnosis of appearance. "Then, preceded by the clear light" means one will experience the arising of the gnosis of the near-attainment of appearance which precedes the clear light. "That is ignorance" refers to the gnosis of the near-attainment of appearance. "At the time when that has gone" means when there are no remaining latent tendencies of that. "Emptiness, extreme emptiness, and great emptiness" are the three natures of appearance and so forth. "By cause and condition" means becoming the substantial cause and the cooperative condition; because one is the cause and the others are the cooperative conditions. "The clear light of those" is because it makes manifest reality which has become the fruit. "The **Great Seal** will be accomplished" means the Vajra Body will arise through the meditative concentration of union. As it is said: "At the time of dawn, through the diamond-like meditative concentration, having sat beneath the Bodhi tree, he destroyed the demons. Emptiness, extreme emptiness, and thirdly great emptiness; the fourth is all-emptiness—these are the distinctions of cause and effect." And also: "The phase of night-appearance is the spreading rays of the sun, the increase of appearance. The juncture is the attainment of appearance, always with its own natures. Neither night, nor juncture, nor day—that which is pure by nature; that is the moment of enlightenment, the field of the supreme master's
<pb n="175"/>
yoga." Thus it appears. In that way, through the stages of external and internal manifest enlightenment, the clear light is experienced and the Vajra Body arising from it is emanated. "Adorned with all the marks" means adorned with the major and minor marks. The "ten powers" are the power of knowing what is possible and impossible, and so forth. The "fearlessnesses" are four; likewise, the "and so forth" refers to being endowed with the qualities of a Buddha, such as the faculties, powers, limbs of enlightenment, and limbs of the path. The distinction of that is the completion of the **Great Seal**, the nature of the body of **Vajrasattva**. Through such phrases, the benefits of attaining reality are shown. "The three realms" means having attained the Buddhahood of the three worlds, one bestows the result of the desired goal. Likewise, the "highly renowned marks" are the unique applications of mindfulness and so forth. Through the phrase "a hundred leagues" <term>yojana</term> and so forth, it is shown that one will illuminate the world-realms of one's own **Infinite Light** <term>Amitābha</term>. Likewise, through the meditative concentration of union, which is the inseparable essence of the conventional and the ultimate, it is shown that one performs the peaceful activities and so forth for the benefit of beings. Through the phrase "just explained" and so forth, the non-transgression of the meditative concentration of the completion stage is shown. Regarding "the practitioner" and so forth, through the meditative concentration of withdrawal via the proximity of the faculties and the sense-objects, the "unlocalized nirvana" which is illustrated by the clear light means the reality of the nature of union. "Peace" means being free from all elaborations. Because the fulfillment of the benefit of others is primary, one should adopt virtue. Because reality is unmistakable, it is "unfailing." The **Compiler** has shown that one will attain the "preeminent," which is the chief among worldly and transcendent accomplishments.
<pb n="176"/>
The summary shows that **Vajradhara**, characterized by the inseparability of the two truths, has spoken through the word "desire" and so forth. "Explained with intention" means reality was shown through the application of contradictory language. From "in that way" and so forth, the minor accomplishments will be explained. From "then" and so forth, the entry into the meditative concentration of **Yamāntaka** <note>The Slayer of Death</note> is shown. Through "the **Tathāgata**" and so forth, the recitation of the mantra of **Yamāntaka** who terrifies the wicked is shown. The explanation of the meaning of the mantra "Oṃ" and so forth is easy to understand. The "interspersing" of the **Yamāntaka** mantra is the application, indicated by the word "to be shown." Then the meaning is this: having shown it, "kill all enemies." Others explain it as the interspersing of the syllable **Hūṃ**; for it is explained: "Kill with the end of **Hūṃ Phaṭ**." Through the phrase "the stalk" and so forth, one focuses on the form of **Yamāntaka** and the others. In a triangular fire-pit possessing fire from thorns, preceded by the recitation of the mantra, one burns poison, blood, salt, mustard seeds, and grain oil while focusing on a girl or an enemy army. If burned at midnight or midday, the text shows "they will be paralyzed within three days." To show that specifically, the phrase "for the sake of the enjoyment associated with girls" is mentioned; for the sake of enjoying the girl's body and for the sake of enjoying her father's "application" <note>wealth/possessions</note>. Therefore, regarding "the practitioner from others," it means she will not go to anyone else but him. Not only that, but as long as she is in the states of childhood, youth, or old age, she will not be happy without him and will be attached to him. Through the phrase "the practitioner of **Vairocana**" and so forth, it is shown that if the thirty-two practitioners of **Vajra Body** and so forth do not respect this application,
<pb n="177"/>
at that time, the beginning of their activity will be meaningless. To show another application, during the "day of the spirits" <note>the 14th or 15th of the lunar month</note>, on a cloth from a cemetery, using charcoal from a cemetery, one should draw the form of **Yamāntaka** inside a union-box <note>two bowls joined together</note> while reciting a hundred and eight times. Having interspersed the name in his heart, preceded by the recitation of the mantra, the practitioner—the yogi who recites the interspersed mantra "Idam dāpaya hrīḥ svāhā" <note>give this [to me], Hrīḥ Svāhā</note> for a specific person a hundred and eight times—will bestow the desired results upon others. Through the phrase "this very mantra" and so forth, one draws the image of the enemy with charcoal on a cemetery cloth. At midday or midnight on the day of the spirits, with the form and mind of a wrathful deity and the thought of sharp weapons, one begins from the head and touches the center down to the circle of the feet. The text shows "the enemy will be stopped" <note>killed</note>. Through the phrase "the hammer" and so forth, one makes an image of the object to be accomplished using the dust from the enemy's feet and earth from both banks of a river. At the previously explained time, the practitioner of **Yamāntaka**, having become angry and reciting the syllable **Phaṭ**, brings the hammer down on its head. At that time, it is shown that "by the hammer falling on the head in actuality, they will be deprived of life." Alternatively, "all these should also be done through meditative absorption," meaning they are performed by meditative concentration alone, so that one does not depend on external substances. Through "Hūṃ" and so forth, one imagines oneself as the King **Vajra-Subjugator** <term>Nīlāmbaradhara-Vajrapāṇi</term> from the transformation of the **Vajra Mind**. In one's own hand, from the transformation of the syllable **Hūṃ**, one imagines a fierce vajra with a garland of flaming **Hūṃ** syllables. As before, one should bring it down on the head of the image of the object to be accomplished. This shows the lack of dependence on external substances. From the phrase "the Vajra Tantra" down to "there is no doubt," the cemetery...

<summary>This section discusses advanced yogic practices from both the generation and completion stages, focusing on the internal and external signs of enlightenment. It details rituals for attaining minor accomplishments and performing subjugation rites using the deity Yamāntaka, emphasizing the power of meditative concentration over external materials.</summary>

<keywords>Yamāntaka, Vajradhara, generation stage, completion stage, four emptinesses, Mahāmudrā, empowerment, tantric ritual, clear light, yoga, mantra</keywords>

The text shows "the enemy will be stopped" <note>killed</note>. Through the phrase "the hammer" and so forth, one makes an image of the object to be accomplished using the dust from the enemy's feet and earth from both banks of a river. At the previously explained time, the practitioner of **Yamāntaka**, having become angry and reciting the syllable **Phaṭ**, brings the hammer down on its head. At that time, it is shown that "by the hammer falling on the head in actuality, they will be deprived of life." ...is taught. Up to this point, the **Compiler** has shown the greatness of the self and the subject matter of the chapter along with the oral instructions. Regarding the phrase "because the body, speech, and mind have become one," it means that if all things are analyzed from the perspective of ultimate reality, they are not perceived as separate. That which dwells in one’s own continuum is precisely what dwells in the continuum of another. However, based on the distinction between the object to be accomplished and the accomplisher, "subjugation" for the sake of reversing adventitious stains means the practitioner subjugates the object to be accomplished. This is also a symbolic term; through peaceful activities and so forth, they are also cared for. Regarding the phrase "A-li Ka-li" <note>vowels and consonants</note> and so forth, it shows the meditative concentration that is beautiful because it completes the collection of activities such as peaceful ones through mantras interspersed with the three syllables <note>Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ</note> which condense all mantras of the nature of the body and so forth. "That which shows it" refers to whatever collection of sounds clarifies it in that way. Regarding "explained with intention," this is because reality is shown through the gateway of contradictory language. From the *Tikā Commentary Clarifying the Lamp* <note>original: "sgron ma gsal bar byེད་ pa'i 'grel pa'i ṭī kā"</note>, this concludes the extensive explanation of the fourteenth chapter.

The explanation of the fifteenth chapter begins with the phrase "The explained and the unexplained" and so forth. The intention is this: what was "explained" was taught in the thirteenth and fourteenth chapters. What was "unexplained" are the collections of activities to be explained in the fifteenth, sixteenth, and seventeenth chapters; because these will not be accomplished without the illusion-like meditative concentration, the fifteenth chapter is taught. Regarding the phrase "possessing the nature of the four emptinesses," these are: emptiness, extreme emptiness, great emptiness, and all-emptiness. Alternatively: appearance, increase of appearance, near-attainment of appearance, and clear light. Alternatively: the four channels within the lotus. The "self" <note>essence</note> is the central channel, the "parasol of desire." As it is said:

"In the center of the <term>bhaga</term> <gloss>source of phenomena/womb</gloss> is the space, adorned with five spaces; possessing a navel and filaments, it is beautiful with eight petals." Thus it appears. Regarding "indestructible," this is because it is the essence of the **Dharma Body**. "All empowerments" refers to the master, the secret, and the wisdom empowerments. The "empowerment of those" refers to the wisdom-gnosis, which is characterized by the phrase "the fourth is likewise." Because he is the essence of that, **Vajradhara** is called "the empowerment of all." All the families divided by the inclinations of sentient beings are the hundred, the five, or the three families. As it is said: "The families are explained as being of a hundred types; condensed, they are of five types; through the division of body, speech, and mind, they later become three types." The **Blessed One**, who is the nature of those, is so because he emanates them. Therefore, the word "knowing" means "emanating." "Indivisible speech" refers to speech characterized by union with a <term>mudrā</term> <gloss>consort/seal</gloss>. "Explained without intention" means showing reality very clearly. "Conduct without proliferation" is the nature of entering into union with a <term>mudrā</term> through the gateway of all such conduct. From the phrase "the outcaste woman" down to "because it is the yoga of conceptualization," it refers to the practitioners of **Akṣobhya**, **Vairocana**, and **Amitābha** in due order. In a place secluded from people, smeared with cow dung and the like, one should draw a wheel of the nature of the support and the supported, or meditate on it with the mind. In its center, one places a well-trained, beautiful, and well-adorned girl of one's own family: an outcaste, a laundry-maid, or a dancer, aged twelve, twenty, or sixteen. They are associated with the blue, red, or white water-lily <note>original: "utpala"</note>, and are pervaded by the five families. Having placed them and preceded by passion and offerings, one should dwell having performed the application <note>of the rites</note> through the stage of withdrawal.

Likewise, the practitioners of **Ratnasambhava** and **Amoghasiddhi** should also dwell having accomplished laundry-maids and outcaste girls, condensed from the families of delusion and hatred. Regarding "the practitioner who has entered thus," it means one who has exerted effort in the conduct without proliferation. "The nature of **Amitābha**" means the text teaches that whoever meditates on the meditative concentration of **Amitābha** will become like him. Since it is a symbolic illustration, it means that the practitioners of **Akṣobhya** and the others will also become like them. "Will dwell on the ten stages" means becoming the master of the ten stages. "Holding the Lord of Speech" shows the benefits of the **Amitābha** yoga. The Lord of Mind and the Lord of Body should be understood for the yogis of **Akṣobhya** and **Vairocana**; likewise, the Treasury of Space and the Performer of All Activities should be explained for the yogis of **Ratnasambhava** and **Amoghasiddhi**. The text shows this by saying "by possessing that yoga, one becomes like that." "Possessing the supreme lordships" means possessing the lordship of the body and so forth. "All sentient beings" means being distinguished from all sentient beings because one is supreme among one's own and other groups. "Becoming a universal monarch" <term>cakravartin</term> means becoming the master of the circle of the mandala. "Because of being a practitioner of the yoga of conceptualization" means by meditating on the generation stage. After showing the divisions of the <term>mudrās</term> of the generation stage yoga in this way, the text then says "it should also be shown to those who dwell in the completion stage." From the phrase "the four families" down to "it will be achieved before long," it shows that a practitioner of the completion stage should take a girl of any of the families, such as a **Brahmin**, and through the sequence of union, experience the three gnoses—appearance and so forth—arising from causes and conditions. One should dwell focusing on the Vajra Body which is the union of the nature of the unlocalized nirvana arising from the stages of manifest enlightenment of the external and internal self.

To show that specifically, "any one of the four families" is said because for those dwelling in the completion stage, there is no conceptualization. "Having taken" means having taken her as a companion in practice. "Possessing that realization" means attaining the deity's body through the completion stage. "That is **Vajradhara**" means because he has become the fruit of everything. "Completing that" means generating the meditative concentration of union. "Having completed it through the stages of manifest enlightenment" means through the two stages. This method is the cause for the accomplishment of the **Great Seal** <term>Mahāmudrā</term>. "When the red boundary is cut and passed" means at dusk, because at that time the sun sets. Therefore, at the time when night falls, the master dwelling in the center of the mandala should perform the ritual of the gathering-circle <term>gaṇacakra</term> with the five types of offerings and so forth, preceded by a prayer for the sake of attaining reality. Then, after the offerings, in the middle of the night, having received the empowerment of wisdom following the secret empowerment from the master who has become pure, one's own family is shown. One "receives empowerment through the arising of bliss." By that very taste, at the time when dawn breaks and the light appears, when the supreme driver of the sun appears, the parts of the night have passed. To show that, "at the time of the rising sun" means first the driver of the sun, the dawn, appears, and then the sun itself rises. At that time, through the instructions on the stages of manifest enlightenment, accomplishment will be attained.

Regarding the "stages of external manifest enlightenment," these are the instructions characterized by the realization of reality in relation to external time. In order to show the internal, the internal stages of manifest enlightenment are taught. "Gnosis of method" is the gnosis of the increase of appearance, named "passion." Because it is illustrated by union, it is the nature of union. "Having arisen" means having generated that. "Setting" means having passed. "Having become the essence of wisdom" refers to the arising and dissolving after the gnosis of appearance. "Then, preceded by the clear light" means one will experience the arising of the gnosis of the near-attainment of appearance which precedes the clear light. "That is ignorance" refers to the gnosis of the near-attainment of appearance. "At the time when that has gone" means when there are no remaining latent tendencies of that. "Emptiness, extreme emptiness, and great emptiness" are the three natures of appearance and so forth. "By cause and condition" means becoming the substantial cause and the cooperative condition; because one is the cause and the others are the cooperative conditions. "The clear light of those" is because it makes manifest reality which has become the fruit. "The **Great Seal** will be accomplished" means the Vajra Body will arise through the meditative concentration of union. As it is said: "At the time of dawn, through the diamond-like meditative concentration, having sat beneath the Bodhi tree, he destroyed the demons. Emptiness, extreme emptiness, and thirdly great emptiness; the fourth is all-emptiness—these are the distinctions of cause and effect." And also: "The phase of night-appearance is the spreading rays of the sun, the increase of appearance. The juncture is the attainment of appearance, always with its own natures. Neither night, nor juncture, nor day—that which is pure by nature; that is the moment of enlightenment, the field of the supreme master's

yoga." Thus it appears. In that way, through the stages of external and internal manifest enlightenment, the clear light is experienced and the Vajra Body arising from it is emanated. "Adorned with all the marks" means adorned with the major and minor marks. The "ten powers" are the power of knowing what is possible and impossible, and so forth. The "fearlessnesses" are four; likewise, the "and so forth" refers to being endowed with the qualities of a Buddha, such as the faculties, powers, limbs of enlightenment, and limbs of the path. The distinction of that is the completion of the **Great Seal**, the nature of the body of **Vajrasattva**. Through such phrases, the benefits of attaining reality are shown. "The three realms" means having attained the Buddhahood of the three worlds, one bestows the result of the desired goal. Likewise, the "highly renowned marks" are the unique applications of mindfulness and so forth. Through the phrase "a hundred leagues" <term>yojana</term> and so forth, it is shown that one will illuminate the world-realms of one's own **Infinite Light** <term>Amitābha</term>. Likewise, through the meditative concentration of union, which is the inseparable essence of the conventional and the ultimate, it is shown that one performs the peaceful activities and so forth for the benefit of beings. Through the phrase "just explained" and so forth, the non-transgression of the meditative concentration of the completion stage is shown. Regarding "the practitioner" and so forth, through the meditative concentration of withdrawal via the proximity of the faculties and the sense-objects, the "unlocalized nirvana" which is illustrated by the clear light means the reality of the nature of union. "Peace" means being free from all elaborations. Because the fulfillment of the benefit of others is primary, one should adopt virtue. Because reality is unmistakable, it is "unfailing." The **Compiler** has shown that one will attain the "preeminent," which is the chief among worldly and transcendent accomplishments.

pages.span: The summary shows that **Vajradhara**, characterized by the inseparability of the two truths, has spoken through the word "desire" and so forth. "Explained with intention" means reality was shown through the application of contradictory language. From "in that way" and so forth, the minor accomplishments will be explained. From "then" and so forth, the entry into the meditative concentration of **Yamāntaka** <note>The Slayer of Death</note> is shown. Through "the **Tathāgata**" and so forth, the recitation of the mantra of **Yamāntaka** who terrifies the wicked is shown. The explanation of the meaning of the mantra "Oṃ" and so forth is easy to understand. The "interspersing" of the **Yamāntaka** mantra is the application, indicated by the word "to be shown." Then the meaning is this: having shown it, "kill all enemies." Others explain it as the interspersing of the syllable **Hūṃ**; for it is explained: "Kill with the end of **Hūṃ Phaṭ**." Through the phrase "the stalk" and so forth, one focuses on the form of **Yamāntaka** and the others. In a triangular fire-pit possessing fire from thorns, preceded by the recitation of the mantra, one burns poison, blood, salt, mustard seeds, and grain oil while focusing on a girl or an enemy army. If burned at midnight or midday, the text shows "they will be paralyzed within three days." To show that specifically, the phrase "for the sake of the enjoyment associated with girls" is mentioned; for the sake of enjoying the girl's body and for the sake of enjoying her father's "application" <note>wealth/possessions</note>. Therefore, regarding "the practitioner from others," it means she will not go to anyone else but him. Not only that, but as long as she is in the states of childhood, youth, or old age, she will not be happy without him and will be attached to him. Through the phrase "the practitioner of **Vairocana**" and so forth, it is shown that if the thirty-two practitioners of **Vajra Body** and so forth do not respect this application,
